record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Characterize the vertices v of a signed graph Σ that belong only to positive circles, meaning that every circle of Σ containing v is positive.

evidence.quote: Questions VP1–4 are V1–4 with the obvious change of "negative" to "positive".
VP4 is easy: v must belong only to balanced blocks.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma=(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a graph (loops and multiple edges allowed) and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ assigns a sign to each edge. A circle (simple closed walk) $C$ in $\Sigma$ is called positive if the product $\prod_{e\in C}\sigma(e)=+1$, and negative otherwise. A signed graph is balanced if every circle in it is positive. A block of $G$ is a maximal connected subgraph with no cut-vertex; a block of $\Sigma$ is balanced if every circle contained in that block is positive.

Characterize the vertices $v\in V$ of a signed graph $\Sigma$ such that every circle of $\Sigma$ passing through $v$ is positive. That is, give a structural characterization of those $v$ for which no negative circle contains $v$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is noted as easy in the original problem collection: a vertex $v$ lies only on positive circles if and only if every block of the underlying graph containing $v$ is balanced. No further research literature is needed; the characterization is immediate from the fact that every circle is contained in a single block.
